newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Malaysian crude OSPs versus Tapis to hold for 1997.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian crude OSPs versus Tapis to hold for 1997.

text.p: Malaysia's state oil company, Petronas, will keep the official price differentials between Tapis and its other crudes steady until the end of 1997, an industry source close to the company said on Tuesday.
Petronas keeps a watching brief on its crude differentials, but was unlikely to change them this year, the source said.
Petronas usually reviews its OSP every six months.
The official selling price (OSP) of Tapis crude is set using the bi-weekly Asia Petroleum Price Index (APPI) quotations and daily reporting services.
The OSPs of its other grades are set at a differential to Tapis.
But a change in APPI, from weekly quotations to bi weekly quotations, has made it more difficult to peg the performance of Malaysian crudes, added the source.
"It would need around a year to assess the data, and see if any adjustment is due," she said.
The last time Petronas adjusted its OSP was in January, when Miri crude was raised to Tapis OSP +10 cents per barrel, compared to -10 cents previously.
This move was criticised by many term buyers at a forum with Petronas held in June because Miri was considered a lower quality crude relative to Tapis.
"But despite the buyers' earlier complaints, there has been more interest for Miri on term in the last few months, so it is unlikely that the differentials will change this year," said the source.
Petronas also adjusted the prices of some of its other crudes in January.
